hardware/docs/revisions.md:55-71: - **Battery polarity: swap J1 and add reverse protection.** Found at bring-up (2026-10-28): every cell Derek has is wired opposite to J1 (pin 1 `BATT_N`, pin 2 `BATT_P`), so the first one went in reversed, and the board got very hot. Afterwards the MAX17048 (U4) answers on I²C but VCELL, SOC and CRATE read 0 with 4.1 V on the cell; it was probably damaged through its VDD/CELL pins. Two changes: * Swap J1's pins to match the packs we actually buy, and keep the + mark. * Add reverse protection after all. B1 relied on the connector and the silkscreen because a high-side PMOS with its gate on board ground doesn't work with the DW01A in the negative lead (board ground is behind Q1). To check: a PMOS in the positive lead with its gate on `BATT_N` (the cell's own negative, ahead of Q1) through a resistor, drain to J1 and source to `BATT_P`. It turns on at Vgs = −Vcell (pick one specified at −2.5 V for an empty cell) and conducts both ways, so the charger still charges through it. R8, the DW01A's supply, would move to the load side so a reversed cell can't drive U3's VCC below its VSS. Work out where the current went in B1 (U2's and U4's substrate diodes, and Q1) before settling on it.
hardware/docs/revisions.md:72-82: - **Add a 5 V aux output.** The power budget leaves ≈1 A at 5 V for LEDs, but nothing brings `+5V_SYS` to a connector: it reaches only regulators, ferrites and capacitors. The only 5 V on a connector is `+5V_A` (audio ribbon pin 10), the codec's filtered analog supply, which LED current would put into the audio. Add a 2-pin JST PH on `+5V_SYS` through a ≈1 A PTC, like the barrel board's LED-strip output (J4). It is the only 5 V still there on battery (the power boards' outputs need an input plugged in), so it suits RGB or bright satellites, which take their LED power from it and their logic from the chain (see the chain contract, §1.4). On B1, a pigtail on a `+5V_SYS` output capacitor (C17, C19 or C22) or FB1's input side stands in. (Found 2026-10-19.)
hardware/docs/revisions.md:84-96: - **CS4272 SDOUT: keep it away from SDIN and SCLK.** Found at bring-up (2026-10-31): the second codec's ADC data takes bursts of corrupted samples, scattered single samples off by up to a quarter of full scale, ~100 to ~1,200 per channel in 10 s, whenever its DAC is also playing. Its DAC side and the Seed's own codec are clean, and with SDIN quiet the ADC side is clean too. `CODEC2_SDOUT` runs ~50 mm on the board 0.15 mm from `CODEC2_SDIN` and `CODEC2_SCLK` on both sides. Slowing the Seed's SAI2 edges changed the count but didn't cure it. Sending the DAC 16-bit words (the low 8 bits zero, as `usb_audio`'s default does) cut it ~100×: 0–10 bad samples per 20 s against 500–1,500 with 24-bit words. Next time: a ground trace or spacing between SDOUT and its neighbours, and source series resistors (~33 Ω) on MCLK, SCLK, LRCK and SDIN at the Seed and on SDOUT at the codec. Check the Seed's codec routing (SAI1) hasn't the same pattern.

instruments/rodeo-001/docs/RODEO_ENCLOSU: ### Aesthetic direction — Cassette Futurism (proposed, for Derek's nod) - **Panel:** **two-layer laser acrylic** — a colored cap over a contrasting core, engraved *through* the cap so labels read in the core color. Earth-tone pairing (e.g. **cream-over- burnt-orange** or **mustard-over-brown**). Period-correct, durable, and the signature Supergraphic look comes free from the engrave-through. (Alt: baltic-birch ply for real-wood warmth — but acrylic holds the 24+ round bushing holes tighter and color-matches the printed cheeks; **my recommendation = two-layer acrylic**.) - **Supergraphics:** bold engraved section-blocks/stripes dividing the 8 zones; chunky 70s sans labels (Moog/ARP/Braun lineage). Optional laser-grid motif framing the OLED window. - **Knobs & cheeks:** skirted fluted 70s-style knobs, earth-tone or black w/ a bright pointer; end-cheeks printed in a matching or contrasting earth tone (wood-fill filament an option). - **Freed constraint:** with the panel non-metal, engraving *is* the labeling (no separate silkscreen step) — plays straight into the cassette-futurist look. **Open for Derek (non-blocking, I'll proceed on the recommendation):** two-layer acrylic vs. plywood panel, and the earth-tone color pairing. Everything else I can dimension now.

rev-a/rodeo-motherboard/docs/RODEO_HUB_I: | **Pull-ups** | **Hub is the Rev-A bus anchor (LOCKED 2026-08-20).** Produced motherboard has none, Daisy's ~40 kΩ internal pulls can't carry the bus, and the HiLetgo SSD1309 has none — so the hub carries **2× 2.2 kΩ, SDA→+3V3 and SCL→+3V3** (Qwiic/MCU +3V3 rail, *not* `LED_3V3`), near J1/J2. **No jumper** (Rev-A space) — safe because every Rev-A hub always pairs with a Rev-A (pull-less) motherboard; both revise to Rev-B together, so a double-pulled bus never happens. Consequence (accepted): OLED shares the bus, so **no hub = no I²C**. Firmware is **indifferent to the anchor** — it only needs valid bus pulls at bring-up. **Rev-B:** pulls move to the motherboard. Bumble owns placement |
